Use this page as the front door to the course. Open a published lesson and its class materials, or scan the planned modules to see where the sequence is going.

::: {.callout-important title="This week: November 16 to 20"}

1. **Monday, Lab 225:** Open the [capacitor slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QKVYTvEYKO5p1Tl6bNlBuRuYwMWiad3VUAgJcsY9Dbg/edit){target="_blank"}. Start at slide 1, play the videos when they appear, and continue through slide 19. Then complete Parts 1 to 4 of the [capacitor notebook](https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/index.html?fromURL=https%3A%2F%2Fandrewandrade.ca%2Ftech-edu-resources%2Fassets%2Ftej-computational%2Fnotebooks%2F10-capacitors-from-zero.ipynb){target="_blank"}. Parts 3 and 4 are short calculation and component-choice challenges.
2. **Tuesday, Portable 1:** Complete the [two-page capacitor charging worksheet](../assets/electronics/worksheets/capacitors-tuesday-worksheet.pdf). Most students begin the prediction and calculation page. Small groups rotate through one teacher-prepared 5 V RC station to charge a real capacitor, measure its voltage every five seconds, and discharge it safely through the resistor. Students waiting for the station can help meter-check and sort components.
3. **Wednesday to Friday:** Finish the capacitor investigation and follow the teacher's directions. The next RC, Tinkercad, and oscilloscope work will be chosen after the available components and meters are checked.

[Open the complete capacitor week page](electronics-library/components/capacitors.qmd).

[Open the component-sorting and RC station notes](circuits/hands-on-circuit-stations.qmd).

:::
